cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the church in Corinth (2 Corinthians 1:1). He makes his appeal by the mildness and gentleness of Christ. Then he calls himself the one who is "humble when face to face with you, but bold when away."
Paul's coming to see them. And there are some people who presume "that we live according to the flesh."

cards.question: When Paul comes to Corinth, what does he beg the Corinthians for?

answers.text: That he won't need to be as bold as he expects
That they'll have the whole church gathered
That they'll find him a place to stay

cards.text: Paul answers that head-on: though we live in the flesh, we don't wage war according to the flesh.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the weapons we fight with are the weapons of the flesh.
Paul says these weapons aren't the weapons of the flesh. Instead, they have ___ power.

cards.text: Those weapons demolish strongholds, and Paul says we demolish arguments and every presumption set up against the knowledge of God. Friend, I once lost an argument to a mixing bowl, and Paul's out here knocking down STRONGHOLDS.

cards.question: Paul says we also take every thought captive. What for?

answers.text: To make it obedient to Christ
To win every debate in town

cards.text: Paul says we'll be ready to punish every act of disobedience, but something has to be complete first. Ready but waiting, friend, that's me in my oven mitts, staring at the timer like it owes me money.

cards.question: Paul says we'll be ready to punish, but only once something is complete. What?

cards.text: Then Paul gets blunt: "You are looking at outward appearances." Friend, that's me grabbing a cookie for its sprinkles and never once checking the dough.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says if anyone is confident he belongs to Christ, he should remind himself that we belong to Christ just as much.

cards.text: Then Paul talks about the authority the Lord gave. Even if he boasts somewhat excessively about it, he says he won't be ashamed.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the authority the Lord gave is for tearing the Corinthians down.

cards.text: Paul doesn't want to seem like he's trying to frighten them by his letters, because some say his letters are weighty and forceful. Friend, Paul's getting a REVIEW, and you just KNOW there's a "but" coming.

cards.question: Paul says some people call his physical presence ___ and his speaking of no account.
Paul tells the people talking about his letters to consider something. What?

answers.text: In person the actions will match the letters
Someone else wrote all of the letters
No more letters are coming to them

cards.text: Now Paul brings up some people who commend themselves. He says we don't dare classify or compare ourselves with them.

cards.question: The people who commend themselves measure themselves by themselves, and Paul says that shows their ___.

cards.text: Measuring yourself by yourself is me judging my cookies against my own cookies, and wow, I win EVERY time! Paul says we will not boast beyond our limits, only within the field of influence God has assigned to us.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says the field God assigned reaches even to the Corinthians.

cards.text: Paul says we aren't overstepping our bounds by counting Corinth in that field.

cards.question: Why does Paul say counting Corinth in that field isn't overstepping?

answers.text: The gospel first reached them through Paul
The other apostles gave Corinth to Paul
Paul was born and raised in Corinth

cards.text: Paul says we don't boast beyond our limits in the labors of others either. But there's a hope for when the Corinthians' faith increases.

cards.question: As the Corinthians' faith increases, what does Paul hope will greatly increase too?

answers.text: The size of their gifts to Paul

cards.question: Why does Paul want his influence among the Corinthians to grow?

answers.text: So he can preach in the regions beyond them
So he can settle down in Corinth for good
So he can lead every church in all of Greece

cards.text: That way, Paul says, we won't be boasting in work already done in another man's territory. Paul is NOT the coworker who presents somebody else's slides and then takes a bow.

cards.question: Paul quotes Jeremiah 9:24: whoever boasts should boast in the ___.
True or false: Paul says the one who commends himself is the one who is approved.

cards.text: Paul says the one who's approved is the one whom the Lord commends. I could stitch "WORLD'S BEST COOKIES" on my own apron, friend, and it's still just me talking.
